findings.description: "ListAgents names them" overstates what the worker can do: ListAgents lists every pup session and the conductor, not the ones that share this worker's files, so for a non-sweep task the hidden N cannot be identified (the peer-joined steer each of them receives is the real mitigation). The line also reads "+1 more sessions" when N is 1.

The 8 peers shown are simply the oldest holding sessions (`listSessions` is `ORDER BY created_at`, and `intersectSessionFiles` keeps that order). The newest sessions, the ones most likely to be editing right now, are the ones folded into "+N more"; ordering by number of shared files or by recency would make the cap keep the most relevant peers.

Decision 99 still says the Peers section lists "each peer by name" (at most 20 files per peer) and that `launchTask` "caps nothing", and its Tests paragraph does not mention the new 8-peer cap or the "+N more" line, so the record and the code now disagree.

The reworded `launchOrRefuse` JSDoc line ("An error the caller could not have avoided — a task already claimed — is printed as a refusal; anything else is a bug and") was joined onto one ~125-character line instead of rewrapped to the ~80-column width of the lines around it.

The comment above `ALLOW_OVERLAP_DESCRIPTION` is now only `// Decision 99.`. That is a bare citation with no WHY, and the constant's text already says overlap is always allowed. AGENTS.md allows comments only for a non-obvious WHY, so delete it, or restore the one-line WHY (the flag is kept for one release so scripts keep working).

The comment above the new 8-peer test restates the `PEERS_SHOWN` JSDoc (the section counts toward the budget, and a launch is never refused), and the `it` title already says "so many broad peers still fit the budget". Delete it.
